defects.claim: A keyboard-off dispatcher that activates first on a shared surface keeps a keyboard-on one from ever taking the keys
defects.scenario: two dispatchers share one surface (the trial camera + instrument case the comment names). The first one attached has `keyboard: false`, so its `src.keys` is false. On a press, its `pointerdown` listener calls `activate(e)`, which adds the event to `CLAIMED` and then calls `actions.activate({ keys: false })`. `ActionsNode.activate` skips `takeKeys` when `keys` is false. The second dispatcher (keyboard on) sees `CLAIMED.has(event)` and returns, so nobody takes the keys. Pressing the surface never gives its shortcuts the keyboard. What should happen: a dispatcher that won't take keys shouldn't claim the event's key activation, or the claim should only be made when keys are actually taken.
defects.cause: claim taken regardless of whether keys are taken

defects.claim: `isEmptyOngoingHandle` treats a handle with only `onWheel` or `cursor` as empty, so the dispatcher drops it
defects.scenario: a held-key action returns `{ onWheel }` from `start`, for "hold a key and scroll to scrub" (the case `OngoingHandle.onWheel` documents). It could also return `{ cursor, subscribe }` to show a mode cursor while the key is held. `isEmptyOngoingHandle` only checks `onMove`, `onEnd`, `overlay`, `previewIds` and `previewPose`, so `invokeAction` reports `'empty-handle'`. The walk then falls through to the next candidate and the handle is never put in flight, so its `onWheel` and `cursor` are never read. `uiOngoing.begin` returns `null` for the same handle. What should happen: any engaged member (`onWheel`, `cursor`, `subscribe`, `previewData`, `previewOpaqueIds`, `kind`) counts as engagement.
defects.cause: incomplete emptiness predicate

defects.claim: A press in a nested surface without the pointer channel is run by the outer dispatcher, but the outer never activates for it
defects.scenario: a surface with `channels.pointer: false` (for example a wheel-only or hover-only overlay) is nested inside a canvas. `holdSurface` counts it in `SURFACES` but not in `POINTER_SURFACES`. On a press inside it, the outer pointer channel's `takesPress` → `pressedNestedIn` sees no pointer surface, so the outer dispatcher runs the drag. The outer's `activate(e)` uses `innermostSurface`, which over `SURFACES` finds the nested element, so it returns without activating. The input scope then goes to the nested surface, or nowhere if the nested one has `keyboard: false`. Keys during the drag (Escape, Delete) don't reach the canvas running it. The wheel path has the same split: in `landedNestedIn` the outer handles the wheel in bubble but doesn't activate. What should happen: who activates for a press and who runs it are decided the same way.
defects.cause: activate and press ownership use different surface maps

defects.claim: The hover cursor override can be written to one sink and cleared from another
defects.scenario: `apply` and `clear` each pick `cursorSink() ?? ownSink` at call time. `cursorSink` is read live because the surface's sink arrives a render after the hook. So a hover before the sink exists writes the override through `ownSink` onto the canvas element's `cursor` style. After the sink arrives, every later `apply`/`clear` goes to the sink. `ownSink`'s override is never cleared, and the stale inline cursor stays on the element until something else overwrites the style. What should happen: an override switching sinks clears the one it last wrote to.
defects.cause: sink chosen per call, not remembered

defects.claim: `explain` reports a keymap's own Escape binding as firing when a plain Escape only closes the keymap
defects.scenario: a keymap is open and binds plain `Escape`; nothing is in flight. `routeThroughKeymap` takes the `isPlainEscape` branch, calls `closeInnermost` and returns `'handled'` without ever calling `passes.run`, so `last` stays null and `routed` falls back to `{ ...ctx, keymapPass: 'only' }` with `fires: false`. `resolveOnly` correctly answers null, but `explain` then walks the `'only'` pass anyway, finds the keymap's Escape binding as `would-fire`, and returns a record with `fired: <that action>` and `outcome: 'handled'`. A real dispatch fires no action (it closes the keymap). The same question gets two different answers in `resolveOnly` and `explain`.
defects.cause: fallback ctx walked when no pass ran

defects.claim: With the pointer channel off, the hover cursor is wiped while a button is held and stays wiped after release until the pointer moves again
defects.scenario: `channels: { pointer: false, hover: true }`. While the pointer rests over an item, the hover cursor shows its action's `cursor`. The user presses and moves: `hover.moved` → `resolve()` sees `pointersHeld() > 0` and applies `inFlightCursor()`, which is `null` because this surface opens no gesture, so the cursor goes back to the default. On release, nothing calls `hover.released` (only `listenPointer` wires it, through the pointer channel's `onUp`), so the cursor stays cleared until the next `pointermove`. It should come back as soon as the button is released, as it does when the pointer channel is on.
defects.cause: no pointerup listener in hover-only mode

defects.claim: In-flight cursor evaluates a function-valued Action.cursor without params, so the mid-gesture cursor can differ from the hover cursor
defects.scenario: An action has a function `cursor` that reads its params, e.g. `cursor: (p) => p?.axis === 'x' ? 'ew-resize' : 'ns-resize'`, and no `activeCursor`. It is bound with `opts.params: { axis: 'x' }`. While hovering, hoverCursor resolves `actionCursor(r.action, r.params)` and shows `ew-resize`. Once the drag starts, `inFlight.cursor()` calls `actionCursor(action)` with no params, so the function gets `undefined` and returns `ns-resize`. A function that dereferences `params` throws instead. The gesture's cursor should be resolved with the params of the binding that opened it.
defects.cause: binding params not kept with the in-flight handle

defects.claim: A multitouch gesture whose opening event lacks an angle never accumulates rotation
defects.scenario: `begin` creates the `turns` entry only when the opening multitouch event has `angle !== undefined`. If the gesture opens on an event without an angle and later moves carry one, `turn()` finds no entry and returns early on every move. `of()` then reports no `rotation`, and `multiTouchOf` falls back to `rotation: 0` for the whole gesture. `turn` has a "gesture that opened on no angle turns from its first one" branch, but it only covers a NaN opening angle, not a missing one. `begin` should seed `{ last: NaN, total: 0 }` whenever the event is multitouch.
defects.cause: turn entry gated on angle presence

defects.claim: explain reports an action as fired for an input that an open keymap withholds
defects.scenario: While a keymap is open and the keystroke's twin was already ruled `taken` (`stack.verdict() === 'taken'`), `routeThroughKeymap` returns `'unhandled'` without calling `run`. `routed` then hands back `{...ctx, keymapPass: 'only'}` with `fires: false`. `explain` still ranks and walks under that pass, so a keymap binding that matches comes back as `winner`. The record has `fired: '<that action>'` and `ranked[..].walk: would-fire`, but `outcome: 'unhandled'`, which is contradictory. A plain Escape the keymap binds is the same case: dispatch closes the keymap, but the record says the keymap's Escape action would fire. When `!route.fires`, `explain` should walk nothing, or report `fired: null`.
defects.cause: walk run under a pass the router never took

defects.claim: A key passed on from the holding dispatcher re-dispatches `over` bindings a peer already tried for that keystroke
defects.scenario: Two dispatchers share one surface. B attached first and has the pointer over it; A holds the keys. On keydown, B's window listener runs first, reaches `{held:false, over:true}` and dispatches its `over` bindings, which come back unhandled. A's listener then declines the key and `passOn` calls `B.take`. That runs `consider` again with `{held:true, over:true}`, so B's `over` bindings are asked a second time. The result is a second trace record, a second `enabled` call and a second `noteRefusal` for the same keystroke. `take` should skip the `over` reach when B's own listener already considered the event, for example by marking events it considered in `taken`.
defects.cause: over reach considered by both own listener and peer offer

defects.claim: `uses` ignores the dispatcher passed to it, so an explicit `on` dispatcher goes unwatched and unsubscribed while it dispatches
defects.scenario: a held key goes down on a view's dispatcher, then that view leaves `views.targets()`. On keyup, `releaseIn` dispatches on `down.on`. `src.uses(d)` runs `redraw.sync(src.dispatchers())`, which leaves `d` out and drops its subscription if it had one. The release's `notify` reaches no `requestRedraw` and no `cursor.changed()`, so the held key's overlay or cursor stays until something else redraws. `DispatchCoreSources.uses` documents that it is "told of the dispatcher each event is about to run on". It should at least watch `d` for the dispatch it is about to run.
defects.cause: argument ignored; sync prunes the dispatcher in use

defects.claim: A drag deferred by its threshold shows its `activeCursor` before the pointer has crossed the threshold
defects.scenario: a press on an action with `dragThresholdPx` (a move that only starts past N px) and an `activeCursor` (`grabbing`). The deferred proxy goes in flight at the press with its `action`. `inFlight.cursor()` falls through `handle.cursor?.()`, which is undefined before start, to `action.activeCursor`. A plain click shows `grabbing` from press to release even though the action never starts. Until `start` runs, the cursor should stay what it was.
defects.cause: cursor read off the action, not the started handle

defects.claim: resolveAll labels an ineligible candidate ranked below the winner `shadowed`, contradicting its contract
defects.scenario: two bindings match a key; the first passes and would fire, the second's action has an `eligible` rule that is false. `resolveAll` (default `evaluateShadowed: false`) reports the second as `{ kind: 'shadowed' }`. `Dispatcher.resolveAll`'s doc (dispatcherApi.ts) says "Nothing is dropped: candidates that resolveOnly's walk would filter out are kept here and labeled `ineligible` instead", and `shadowed` means "never asked". Eligibility was already evaluated in `rank` (`r.eligible`), so the rule's verdict is known and free; an inspector showing why a binding is dead reads "shadowed" for an action that could never fire in this context.
defects.cause: ineligible branch gated on `fired && !evaluateShadowed`

defects.claim: immediateRunParams lets the dispatcher's `viewId` and `roles` overwrite the binding's own params
defects.scenario: a binding declares `opts.params: { viewId: 'minimap' }` (or a `roles` param) for an immediate action. `immediateParams` spreads `resolved` last so the binding wins, as `ImmediateParams`' doc promises ("beneath the binding's own params, which win on a clash"), but `immediateRunParams` then assigns `params.viewId = run.viewId` and `params.roles = …` after it, so the binding's value is silently replaced. The same function feeds drop previews (dropPreview.ts), so both paths disagree with the documented precedence.
defects.cause: post-spread assignment ignores the binding-wins rule

defects.claim: Tearing down a listener set mid-drag leaves the pointer pinned in the view resolver, so later hovers route to the stale view
defects.scenario: a surface with `views` (a viewport panel). The mouse (pointerId 1) presses in view A; `routeDown` calls `resolver.begin(1, …)`, which pins 1 → A. Before release the listener set re-binds (a `keyboard`/channel/`yieldKeys` change, or `enabled` toggled). `attachInput`'s teardown sets `disposed = true`, then `pointer.dispose()` cancels each session. `onCancel` returns early on `core.disposed()` before `routeRelease`, and `dispose` never calls it either, so `resolver.end(1)` never runs. The resolver outlives the listener set (it comes from `views`). In the new listener set, each unpressed mouse move goes through `onHoverMove → onMove → routeAt(1, …)`, and `ViewResolver.at` hands back the pinned view A wherever the pointer is. So `hover` events (and their `affordanceAt`/`classifyTarget` hit tests and world points) run on view A's dispatcher and camera until the next press re-pins. It should unpin every pointer held at teardown.
defects.cause: teardown skips routeRelease for held pointers

defects.claim: In a text field, an AltGr-typed character counts as a Ctrl chord, so an `inFields` Ctrl+Alt binding swallows the typed character
defects.scenario: on a German layout, typing `@` (AltGr+Q) in an input reports `ctrlKey` and `altKey` with key `@`. `fieldChord` sees `ctrlKey` and lets the key through as a chord, and the field branch dispatches it with `typedMods(e)` (the real Ctrl+Alt). The `typedWithAltGraph` handling that the non-field path uses is never applied here. A binding declaring `inFields` that matches Ctrl+Alt+`@` (or one matching on `code` KeyQ with Ctrl+Alt) fires and calls `preventDefault`, so the `@` never reaches the field. In a field, a keystroke AltGr typed is text, and `fieldChord` should exclude it (`typedWithAltGraph(e)`).
defects.cause: fieldChord ignores AltGraph

defects.claim: One pointer leaving the canvas clears pointer-over while another pointer is still over it
defects.scenario: on a touch laptop the mouse rests over the canvas and the user holds a key for an `over` binding, which is engaged. A finger taps the canvas. When it lifts, the touch pointer's `pointerleave` runs `setPointerOver(false)` and `keys.leave()`, so the `over` binding is released and later keys are not heard as over, although the mouse never left. The same happens when a pen leaves while the mouse stays. The flag is one boolean for every `pointerId`, with no count or set of pointers that are over the canvas.
defects.cause: per-surface flag, not per-pointer

defects.claim: A key pressed before Cmd and released while Cmd is down is never released, so it stays held forever
defects.scenario: Hold Space (a key-held hand pan starts; `heldKeys` records `withCmd: false` because Cmd was not down at keydown), press Cmd, release Space, release Cmd. macOS suppresses the keyup of a key released while Cmd is down, so the Space keyup never arrives; Cmd's keyup then releases only entries with `withCmd` set, which Space's is not. The hand gesture and the `downKeys` entry stay engaged until Space is pressed again (autorepeat of nothing, a later `arrive` re-presses Space for `over` bindings). It should be released with Cmd's keyup like a key pressed during Cmd. `withCmd` is captured only at the key's own keydown; a Meta keydown never marks the keys already down.
defects.cause: withCmd sampled only at the key's own keydown

defects.claim: A keymap leader held before Cmd is never released by Cmd's keyup, so it stays held
defects.scenario: A leader key opens a hold keymap (`holdOpened`), recorded with `e.metaKey` false. Cmd goes down, the leader is released (no keyup on macOS), Cmd is released: `up` releases only leaders with `withCmd` true, so `stack.release('key:<physical>')` never runs and the hold keymap stays open until something else closes it.
defects.cause: withCmd sampled only at the leader's keydown

defects.claim: The hover cursor leaves a stale live prediction on the trace after recording stops
defects.scenario: While the trace records, each idle resolve calls `ctx.trace.setLive(() => d.explain(press, ctx))`. When the watcher releases (`recording()` turns false) nothing calls `setLive(null)` (only `clear()` does, on leave/teardown), so the closure keeps the last press point, ctx and dispatcher. A devtools panel that starts watching again reads `trace.live()` before the next pointer move and gets an `explain` run against the old point and an old context snapshot, which can name an action that no longer wins. Should withdraw (`setLive(null)`) when not recording, or set it regardless of `recording()`.
defects.cause: live explain set only while recording, never withdrawn

defects.claim: An exception thrown by an ongoing handle's onMove or onWheel escapes dispatch, while throws from start, run and onEnd are caught
defects.scenario: An action whose `onMove` throws on some move: `invokeAction` catches throws from `start`/`run` and `runOnEnd` catches `onEnd`, but `pumpGesture` calls `handle.onMove` (pointermove, multitouch, carry) and `handle.onWheel` bare. The throw propagates out of `handleInput` into the pointer channel's `onMove`, so `opts.hover.moved(e)` is skipped for that event (cursor and hover dispatch go stale) and, on the keyboard/wheel paths, `preventDefault`/`stopImmediatePropagation` are never reached, so the page scrolls or zooms under a claimed wheel. The gesture stays in flight with no log naming the action. Should be caught and logged as the other handle callbacks are.
defects.cause: missing try/catch around handle callbacks in the pump

defects.claim: An ongoing action started from a click, double click or context menu gets no drag.affordance even though the event carries the hit
defects.scenario: an ongoing action bound to `contextmenu` or `click` over a handle (the event's `affordance` is filled by `underPointer` in contextMenu.ts and the recognizer) reads `ctx.drag.affordance` in `start` and finds `undefined`, because `pressDrag` copies the affordance only for `pointerdown`. `InvocationCtx` has no other place that carries the hit, so the action can't tell which handle it was started on. The immediate path gets it through `landed()` in inputFacts.ts, so the two paths answer the same question differently. The affordance should be copied for every kind `pressDrag` handles.
defects.cause: kind check narrower than the kinds handled

defects.claim: With keyboard: 'page', keydown is heard on the canvas's own document but keyup, blur and paste only on the global window
defects.scenario: a canvas rendered into another document (an iframe or a `window.open` popout through a portal) with `keyboard: 'page'`. Its keydowns go to `canvas.ownerDocument`, so a key-held binding (Space for the hand tool) starts. The keyup listener is on the hook's global `window`, which never sees that document's keyup, and the blur listener is on the same wrong window. The held gesture and the `heldKeys` entry then stay engaged until something else cancels them. keyup and blur should be heard on `ownerDocument.defaultView`, the same window the keydown target belongs to.
defects.cause: one listener target derived from the canvas, the rest hard-wired to window

defects.claim: A binding to an unregistered action warns on every input, including every pointer move for a hover binding
defects.scenario: a contribution binds `{ kind: 'hover' }` (or a key that autorepeats) to an action id that is not registered. `dispatcher.hover` walks with an `attempt` on every mouse move, so `console.warn("binding resolved actionId … Skipping")` fires once per move with no dedupe, where the misbound case right beside it (`reportMisbound` in gestureRun.ts) reports once per action. The console floods.
defects.cause: warning not deduplicated

defects.claim: A drop whose items fail to materialize, or whose dispatch throws, becomes an unhandled promise rejection
defects.scenario: `void itemsFromDataTransfer(dt).then(...)` has no rejection handler. When reading a dropped file rejects (a permission error, a folder entry), or the action's invoker throws synchronously inside `dispatch` (an immediate invoker's throw is caught, but an ongoing `start`'s path or a keymap effect is not), the rejection surfaces as an unhandledrejection with no "weasel dispatcher" context. Every other dispatch path logs through `console.error` with the action named.
defects.cause: missing .catch on the materialization promise

defects.claim: The claimKeys effect takes the keys even when the dispatcher's keyboard channel is off
defects.scenario: a mount with `keyboard: false, claimKeys: true` calls `actions.activate()` with no options, and the default is `keys: true`. This takes the page's keys away from another canvas, but this dispatcher binds no key listeners, so the keys go nowhere. Every pointerdown and wheel activation passes `{ keys: src.keys !== false }` (dispatchCore.ts `activate`), so the same decision is answered two ways. What should happen: the mount effect passes `{ keys: keyboard !== false }`, as the core does.
defects.cause: activate option dropped on one path

defects.claim: A pointer release that yields to an item's own session skips re-resolving the hover cursor
defects.scenario: with `controls` or a nested item session, a press whose item took it is released before it moves. `claims.yielded` is true, so `onUp` calls `onCancel` and returns before `opts.hover.released(e)`. The cursor shown while the pointer was held (`inFlightCursor()`, `null` in this case) stays until the next move. What should happen: the cursor is re-resolved at the release point, as on the normal path.
defects.cause: early return skips hover.released

defects.claim: A WebKit pinch re-routes on every change event, so a pinch drifting across views switches to another view's dispatcher mid-gesture
defects.scenario: on a surface with several views, a trackpad pinch starts over view A. `onGestureStart` probes A's bindings and claims the gesture. Each `gesturechange` calls `routeAt(null, cx, cy)` on its focal point. If the focal point crosses into view B, the remaining scale steps dispatch on B's dispatcher and zoom B, which never claimed the start. B may have no pinch binding at all, in which case the steps still get preventDefault'd because `pinchLive` is set. A pointer drag (`routeDown`) and a carry (`pinned` in carry.ts) are both pinned to the view they began in. The pinch, also a continuous gesture, is not.
defects.cause: no view pin for the pinch stream

defects.claim: Autorepeat stays swallowed for a held key after its gesture has been ended under it
defects.scenario: Space is held for the hand tool, so `heldKeys` has it. A tool switch or `cancelAll` (Escape, window-level cancel) ends that gesture while Space stays down. Each autorepeat then hits `heldKeys.has(physical)`, which calls `preventDefault` and returns, so the hold never re-engages and the page never sees the key until it is released. `followPointer.arrive` answers the same question with `stillHeld` (whether the gesture is still in flight) and presses such a key again. The two places decide "is this key still held" differently.
defects.cause: map presence used instead of in-flight check

defects.claim: A wheel over a nested surface whose wheel channel is off is handled by the outer surface, which never activates for it
defects.scenario: An inner dispatcher sets `channels.wheel: false` but is still counted by `holdSurface`. A wheel landing in it reaches the outer surface's bubble listener (`landedNestedIn`), and the outer dispatcher dispatches and claims it. `core.activate(e)` refuses, though, because the event landed in the inner surface. No one activates a scope for that wheel, so the keys stay wherever they were, even though the outer surface acted on the input. Activation should go to the surface that actually handles the wheel.
defects.cause: activation decided by landing surface, not by the surface that listens for the channel

defects.claim: DispatchRecord.matched is not in matcher order when a claim barred some bindings
defects.scenario: `DispatchRecord.matched` is documented as "every binding whose spec matched the input, in matcher order". The code builds it as `[...r.ordered, ...r.barred]`, so every barred binding comes after all admitted ones, whatever its scope tier and specificity. It is also listed after the reordering done by `preferViewScoped` and `preferContextual`. A devtools reader comparing positions sees a hotkey-tier barred binding below an ambient admitted one.
defects.cause: doc/code mismatch on ordering

defects.claim: A paste the key-holding dispatcher declines is never offered to the other dispatchers on its surface, unlike a key
defects.scenario: two dispatchers on one surface: a trial camera and an instrument on another registry. A keystroke the one holding the keys declines goes to the peer through `passOn` (keyPeers.ts). A paste returns early at `if (!core.holdsKeys()) return;` on the peer, and the holder dispatches it and gets nothing. A `paste` binding on the peer never fires, while a Cmd+V `key` binding on the same peer would. The routing question "who on this surface may take page input the holder declined" gets two different answers.
defects.cause: paste bypasses the surface peer list

defects.claim: The hover cursor's live trace prediction goes stale while the pointer is over an affordance and while a gesture is in flight
defects.scenario: devtools are recording, and the pointer moves from open canvas onto a resize handle whose affordance carries a `cursor`. `resolve` returns at the affordance branch (and at the held/in-flight branch above it) before `ctx.trace.setLive(...)`. So `trace.live()` keeps explaining a press at the previous, off-handle point, which is the wrong action for where the pointer now rests. It should set (or withdraw) the live record on every resolve that changes the point.
defects.cause: setLive skipped on early returns

defects.claim: The hover cursor checks for an in-flight gesture only on the routed view's dispatcher, so a gesture running on another dispatcher is missed
defects.scenario: on a surface with views, a key-held ongoing gesture starts on view A's dispatcher (for example an `over` key binding), and the pointer, with no button held, then moves into view B. `resolve` routes to B, reads `dispatcherNow().inFlight().size === 0`, and shows B's idle prediction instead of A's `inFlightCursor`. `changed()` likewise sets `flying` from B's dispatcher alone, so when A's gesture ends nothing triggers `refreshSoon`. Expected: in-flight state is read across `src.dispatchers()` (or the dispatcher that holds the gesture), as `cancelAll` on teardown already does.
defects.cause: per-view in-flight check

defects.claim: A pointer cancel ends its drag with a context at world (0,0) and no `drag` or trail
defects.scenario: a drag is in flight and the recognizer dispatches `{ kind: 'pointercancel', pointerId, …mods }`, which carries no x/y (gestures/src/ui/inputEvent.ts:168). Examples are a session cancel, window blur (`cancelHeld`), or a lost capture. `endGesture` builds the onEnd context with `buildInvocationCtx`. `worldPointOf` has no `pointercancel` case and returns undefined, so `world` is `{0,0}`. `pumpDrag` runs only for `pointermove`/`pointerup`, so `ctx.drag` is absent: no start, no delta and no `points`. gestureFacts' contract says `onEnd` "is handed the same trail". An onEnd that reads `ctx.drag` on cancel (to revert to `drag.start`, or to finish a lasso from `drag.points`) gets undefined, or throws, where a commit would get the trail. The cancel context should be built from the gesture's facts: its origin and its last sampled point.
defects.cause: pointercancel not given drag facts

defects.claim: A keystroke inside a held keymap is marked as having closed the keymap, so its autorepeat is dropped
defects.scenario: Hold a leader key that opens a keymap with `holdOpened`, then press and hold an arrow bound inside it (a nudge). The first input seen while held runs `markUsed`, which rebuilds `levels` and `notify()` rebuilds `snapshot` as new frozen objects. The keymap is still open, but `s.innermost() !== before` compares object identity, so it reads as changed and `quiet.set(physical)` runs. `consider` then `preventDefault`s and drops every repeat of that arrow, so holding it nudges once instead of repeating. The same happens on a `swallowed()` keystroke, which also calls `markUsed` and then notifies. It should only go quiet when the innermost keymap actually changed (compare id and stack depth, or check that `before` is no longer open).
defects.cause: identity compare of rebuilt snapshot

defects.claim: A pointer release after the hover has already left the canvas re-shows the cursor and the painted pointer off the canvas
defects.scenario: With `controls: 'take'`, press a control near the canvas edge. That session is uncaptured until it passes `dragPx`. Move off the canvas before reaching the threshold: `pointerleave` fires, so `onLeave` runs `clear()` and sets `last = null`. Release outside. The session's `onEnd` calls `hover.released(e)`, which sets `last` to the outside point and schedules `refreshSoon`. That `refresh` routes, applies a hover cursor override, and calls `painted.setPointer` at a point outside the canvas, and it can set the trace's live prediction. No second `pointerleave` arrives to clear it, so the painted cursor and override stay until the pointer comes back. `moved` from session moves outside the canvas does the same. Expected: nothing is shown for a pointer that has left.
defects.cause: `released`/`moved` ignore that the pointer left

defects.claim: A canvas-less dispatcher misses React Aria-style modals, so page keys fire behind the dialog
defects.scenario: a modal that marks the page `inert`/`aria-hidden` instead of setting `aria-modal` (React Aria, as the doc comment says) counts as modal only through `canvas !== null && hiddenBehind(canvas)`. A dispatcher with no canvas (`usePageActions`, or any `canvasRef` resolving to null with `keyboard: 'page'`) passes `canvas === null`, so `inModalOver` returns false. A shortcut key pressed while focus is on a button inside such a dialog then reaches the page's actions behind it. An `aria-modal="true"` dialog or a native modal `<dialog>` does block the same dispatcher, so whether a modal blocks page keys depends on how the dialog library marks it. With no canvas, the check should fall back to whether the dialog's surroundings are inert or hidden (for example, whether the document body outside the dialog is).
defects.cause: inert check keyed only on the canvas

defects.claim: A wheel during a drag reaches only the dispatcher of the view under the pointer, not the one running the drag
defects.scenario: on a surface with several views, start a drag in view A, move the pointer over view B and scroll. `onWheel` routes with `routeAt(null, …)` to B, so `dispatch` runs on B's dispatcher. `pumpGesture` offers the wheel to `inFlight.handles` of that dispatcher only, so A's in-flight handle never sees it and its `onWheel` claim (meant to let a drag consume the wheel) is skipped; the wheel zooms or scrolls B under a live drag in A instead. A held pointer stays pinned to its view for every other channel (`routeAt(pointerId…)`), but the wheel isn't pinned.
defects.cause: wheel routed by position, ignoring pinned in-flight drags

defects.claim: Hover facts go stale through a press nothing hears, so the hover-off and the next `from` name the pre-press spot
defects.scenario: when a pointer is held and no binding hears held hovers, `moved` skips `hoverAt`, so `facts` keeps the position and hit from before the press. If the drag then ends with the pointer outside the canvas, `pointerleave` runs `onLeave`, which dispatches `hover { off: true }` at the old `facts.at`, with `where` (affordance, body) from before the press. A hover binding tracking enter and leave gets told the pointer left from a place it last saw minutes ago. In the same way, the first hover after release carries a `from` naming the pre-press hit rather than where the pointer actually came from. `facts` should be dropped (or refreshed) when a press begins, or at release.
defects.cause: facts not invalidated while unheard

defects.claim: resolveAll returns no candidates for an input that an open keymap passes on when nothing in the keymap pass fires
defects.scenario: a keymap is open; a Ctrl/Cmd chord, a bare modifier, Tab, or a cascaded key is passed on with `run('none', …)`. Every candidate in that pass is disabled (`enabled()` refuses). `routed` reports `fires: false` because the pass was unhandled, and `resolveAll` returns `[]` at `if (!route.fires) return []`. With no keymap open the same input lists each candidate with a `disabled` verdict. The doc says only an input the keymap *withholds* (a key it swallows, a press kept for a click) lists none; an input passed on and merely unhandled should still list its candidates with their verdicts.
defects.cause: "not fired" conflated with "withheld by the keymap"

defects.claim: A drag that is handed off is re-ranked without keymap routing
defects.scenario: a keymap is open and a press was routed through `routeThroughKeymap` (pass `'only'`, then `'none'`). The drag's handle returns `'pass'` from `onMove`. `handOff` calls `rank(press, ctx, …)` with the move's ctx, where `keymapPass` is undefined. `assembleScopedBindings` then puts the keymap's entry bindings in alongside every other binding. So the drag can go to a candidate that neither of the press's passes would have offered, such as a keymap binding the `'none'` pass excludes. Expected: the hand-off offers the same candidates the press's own routing did.
defects.cause: hand-off re-ranks without the keymap pass the press ran under

defects.claim: Immediate params for wheel and pinch drop the bodyTarget and bodyKind the event carries
defects.scenario: the wheel and pinch channels spread `underPointer(...)` onto the event, so it carries `bodyTarget`/`bodyKind` (wheel.ts:50, webkitPinch.ts:63). `carried()` copies only `affordance` for these two kinds. An immediate wheel action, for example "scroll a hovered node's value", reads `params.bodyTarget` and gets undefined. Click, press, contextmenu and hover pass the same fields through `landed()`. The option is silently dropped on one path.
defects.cause: wheel/pinch branches omit fields landed() copies

defects.claim: A non-modal ARIA dialog is treated as modal whenever any ancestor of the canvas is aria-hidden or inert
defects.scenario: the canvas sits inside a wrapper that has `aria-hidden="true"` for an unrelated reason (a decorative or offscreen container, or a closed drawer marked inert). A non-modal `role="dialog"` popover elsewhere has focus, with no `aria-modal`. `hiddenBehind(canvas)` is true, so `inModalOver` reports a modal. Keys and pastes typed in the popover are dropped by the keyboard and ingest channels, although nothing modal is open. The check cannot tell whether *this* dialog caused the hiding.
defects.cause: inert/aria-hidden heuristic not tied to the dialog

defects.claim: Wheel and WebKit pinch send a view's camera the focal point in canvas coordinates instead of view-local ones, so zoom drifts
defects.scenario: A CanvasView sits at canvas x=100 and the user zooms at canvas x=150 (view x=50). Going from 1× to 2× leaves the camera at x=75 instead of x=25, so the point under the pointer drifts
defects.cause: focal point not mapped to view-local coordinates

defects.claim: A surface leave reports the last hover hit from one view but dispatches on the currently routed view, so the hovered view's leave binding never fires
defects.scenario: Hover over view A to open an overlay, then wheel over view B without a hover sample there, then leave the surface. A's overlay is never cleared
defects.cause: hover facts don't record the view they came from

defects.claim: The drop preview cache key leaves out resolved binding params, so a stationary OS drag keeps a stale preview after the params change
defects.scenario: Change a setting that a thunked param reads while the drag is held still. The next dragover keeps the old preview, but the drop invokes with the new params
defects.cause: preview key omits params

defects.claim: An open keymap takes an inFields chord typed in a text field ahead of the ordinary field-enabled binding
defects.scenario: A page Ctrl+S and a keymap Ctrl+S both set inFields: true. With the keymap open and a text field focused, Ctrl+S runs the keymap's action instead of the page's
defects.cause: keymap routing not excluded for field reach

defects.claim: A hover over a nested dispatcher surface is also routed, hit-tested and given a cursor by the outer surface
defects.scenario: a panel that runs its own dispatcher sits inside a canvas that runs another. The pointer moves over the panel. The panel's `pointermove` bubbles to the outer canvas, whose `onHoverMove` → `onMove` → `hover.moved` hit-tests the outer scene under the panel, dispatches `hover` events to the outer bindings (a hover highlight on whatever lies under the panel), and resolves and paints the outer cursor (including a painted cursor through `setPointer`). `trackPointerOver` also keeps the outer `pointerOver` true, so the outer surface's `over` key bindings fire alongside the panel's. Presses get the nesting check (`pressedNestedIn`), and so do wheel, contextmenu, pinch and drop (`landedNestedIn`/`eventTaken`), but hover and `over` do not. What should happen: a move that landed in a nested surface is treated like a leave for the outer one.
defects.cause: no nesting check on hover/over

defects.claim: An over-held key whose gesture was ended elsewhere is never removed from `held` on leave
defects.scenario: Space taken by an `over` binding, then the gesture is ended by `cancelAll` (tool switch, Escape) while Space stays down. On pointer leave, `releaseIn` finds nothing in flight and returns 'unhandled', so the entry stays in `held` (`heldKeys`). Until Space's keyup arrives, `consider` treats every autorepeat as a key "already engaged": it calls preventDefault and skips dispatch, so an ordinary `key` binding on Space (or the page's own default) never sees the repeats. The same stale entry follows any held key whose gesture `cancelAll` ends. What should happen: the entry is dropped whenever its gesture is no longer in flight (`stillHeld` false), not only when the release is handled.
defects.cause: removal gated on release outcome rather than liveness

defects.claim: With a keymap open, prediction calls `enabled()` one more time than the dispatch it predicts, so its verdict can differ from what dispatch does
defects.scenario: a keymap is open and the hover cursor calls `resolveOnly(press)` per move. `routed` runs `routeThroughKeymap`, whose `run` callback already walks (asking `enabled()` on the candidates) to learn whether the pass fires; then `resolveOnly` / `resolveAll` / `explain` walk the same ranked context again, asking every gate a second time. `ResolveAllOptions.evaluateShadowed`'s doc promises that the default walk keeps `resolveOnly`'s `enabled()` call count identical to a real dispatch, which walks each pass once. Expected: keep the walk `routed` already made (its `Walked`) and reuse it rather than walking again.
defects.cause: walk result of the keymap pass discarded and recomputed

defects.claim: A nested surface with `contextMenu: false` still has its native context menu taken by the outer surface
defects.scenario: an outer canvas with the contextmenu channel on contains an inner dispatcher surface that set `channels.contextMenu: false` ("Off leaves the browser's native menu in place"). A right-click inside the inner surface fires `contextmenu`, which bubbles to the outer listener. That listener calls `preventDefault()` unconditionally before anything else; `eventTaken` is false because the inner surface has no listener, so the outer also routes and dispatches the right-click on its own bindings. The native menu never opens over the inner surface. Wheel (`landedNestedIn`) and pointerdown (`pressedNestedIn`) both check for a nested surface; this channel doesn't. Expected: leave an event that landed in a nested surface without the channel to the browser, or at least don't suppress its default before knowing whether anything here takes it.
defects.cause: no nested-surface check before the unconditional preventDefault

defects.claim: When the two fingers of a pinch land in different views, the first finger's moves are dropped
defects.scenario: on a surface with several views, finger A goes down in view 1 (pinned there by `routeDown`), and finger B goes down in view 2. B's press runs `claimForMultiTouch` while routed to view 2, so the multitouch handle opens on view 2's dispatcher. Then A moves: `onMove` → `routeAt(A, …)` routes to view 1, and the recognizer's `sink.multiTouchInFlight(2)` asks `core.dispatcherNow()` (view 1), which has nothing in flight, so no multitouch event goes out for A's moves. Only B's moves drive the pinch, so the spread and centroid update only when B moves. Expected: a multitouch gesture runs on the one view it opened in, whichever finger moves.
defects.cause: multitouch routed per finger's pin, not per gesture

defects.claim: Rebinding the input listeners cancels ongoing handles started from the UI, not just pointer gestures
defects.scenario: A color slider is mid-scrub through `actions.begin(...)`, which is `beginUiOngoing` on the dispatcher SceneCanvas shares. Anything that re-runs the attach effect fires the teardown: toggling `enableKeybindings` (→ `keyboard`), any `channels` flag, or `yieldKeys`. The teardown calls `d.cancelAll('cancel')` on every dispatcher. `cancelAll` also clears `uiOngoing` and cancels the slider's handle, so the scrub is reverted even though no pointer, key or gesture of these listeners was involved. The teardown only needs to end gestures its own listeners would never see end (pointer, key-held, carry). The UI-driven `ui-*` handles should be left alone.
defects.cause: cancelAll used as a teardown-scoped cancel

defects.claim: A drag that crosses a child element of the canvas fires dragleave, which tears down the drop preview and rebuilds it
defects.scenario: The surface element has children (overlay layers, HUD). An OS file drag moves from the element onto a child. Where the engine gives `dragleave` a null `relatedTarget` (Safari has historically done this), the guard fails, so the class is removed and `preview.end()` runs. The next `dragover` then calls `show` with `key` reset, which starts `action.preview` again. The preview flickers and restarts at every child boundary. The fix is to count enter/leave depth, or to treat a null `relatedTarget` as unknown and leave the end to the next `dragover` that finds no winner.
defects.cause: relies on relatedTarget for containment
